title: Checkpoints, recovery and outages

story: Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, is building RH-1234 on a full VM. Steps 1 to 3 are done and their tests pass: the code was read, the failing tests are written, the empty-state card exists. In the middle of step 4, hiding the card while the table is loading, the VM freezes. The harness is our program inside the VM that runs the Claude session, and its heartbeat, a small "I'm alive" message it sends every 30 seconds, stops arriving.

Two hours of work happened on that machine. If the code, the notes and the conversation lived only on its disk, Nova would start again from zero, and you would answer the same question twice. And if the next VM freezes too, should Nova try a third, a fourth, a tenth time?
hook.question: How do we lose only the unfinished part of step 4 when a VM dies, and when do we stop trying and call a person?

read.h: Save outside the machine after every good step
p: The rule behind this lesson is that the VM is only a workbench. Everything worth keeping is saved somewhere else while the run works, so a dead machine costs minutes, not a ticket. The moment to save is a checkpoint: after each step whose checks pass, the harness, our program inside the VM that runs the Claude session, commits the work and pushes it to the run's branch through the broker, the service that holds our GitHub, Jira and Slack credentials and makes those calls for the run. A checkpoint after a good step is a point we can always start again from, because its tests passed.

Three kinds of things leave the machine. The code goes to the branch nova/RH-1234 as a commit called wip(RH-1234): <step> [skip ci]. The memory goes to the runs bucket, the S3 bucket that keeps each run's files: notes.md, the plan, decisions, what is done and what is next in plain words, plus a small record that ties the step to its commit and session. The conversation is already safe, because the session store from the harness lesson mirrors it as it goes. Finally, the heartbeat carries the checkpoint's commit sha, so the orchestrator, our Temporal worker that follows the run, always knows the latest safe point.

notes.text: git diff --quiet exits with 1 when something is staged, so the promise rejects and we know there is something to commit.
[skip ci]: backend CI runs on a push to any branch and would take the QA locks, the shared test environment that backend CI reserves, at every checkpoint. The commit that opens the PR has no marker.
Never a force push: the broker refuses a push that moves the branch backwards.
The orchestrator learns the latest safe commit from the heartbeat, without asking the VM.

read.h: A dead VM is replaced, never repaired
p: On the orchestrator side, the activity that follows the harness is workInSandbox. When five minutes pass with no heartbeat, or AWS says the machine failed its status check, it gives up on the VM and throws an error of the type SandboxDead. The heartbeat comes from a timer in nova-worker, not from the model, so a long thinking turn is never mistaken for death.

runWithRecovery is the loop around a sandbox step. It claims a VM, freshens it (checks out the code at a given commit) at the last checkpoint instead of at main, and resumes from the next step. If the step throws SandboxDead, the finally block destroys that VM, and the loop claims a fresh one from the warm pool, the stopped VMs that wait already set up. A dead VM is never reused, because nobody knows what state it is in. Any other error is a real failure and goes up to the caller unchanged.

notes.text: The last checkpoint if there is one, otherwise the main commit the plan was made on.
resumeFrom gives the harness the session id and the notes, so it continues with step 4, not step 1.
LabNotReady (FCP Lab would not start) is treated like a lost VM: one more try on a fresh machine.
handBack posts this message in the thread and on the ticket, and makes the requester the assignee again, like every ending of a run.

read.h: The second loss calls a person
p: Why stop at two? One frozen VM is bad luck: machines fail, and a fresh one usually works. Two in a row on the same ticket is a pattern. Maybe step 4 starts a test that uses all the memory, maybe the ticket asks for something that crashes FCP Lab. A third VM would most likely die the same way, and the run would become an expensive loop that nobody is watching.

So the second loss ends the run as needing a person, and like every ending of a run it hands the ticket back. The message, in the thread and on the ticket, says where the work is: the branch with every checkpoint and the notes in the runs bucket. The requester becomes the assignee again, so the Jira poll does not start the same work a minute later. Nothing is thrown away, and the person who looks starts from step 4, not from zero. This is the same idea you will meet again in the progress watcher: the platform does not limit how long a run may take, but it notices when trying again has stopped making sense.

deeper.h: Go deeper: Spot machines and outages
p: Nova runs on normal on-demand machines because it waits for people, but routines such as the CI fixer use cheaper Spot machines, which AWS can take back with a two-minute warning. The harness listens for that warning, runs nova-worker checkpoint and exits as preempted, and the workflow retries the step on a fresh VM from that checkpoint. It is the same recovery as a frozen VM, only with a warning first.

Outages of the services around the run get the same treatment: wait, do not lose work. The SDK retries a failing model call itself; if Claude is still unavailable after 15 minutes, the harness checkpoints and exits as paused_outage, the workflow parks the VM and tries again after 15 minutes, 30 minutes, then every hour. Messages to people go through notify, which posts in the Slack thread, or as a Jira comment when Slack is down, and the other way round. When the broker or the gateway is down nothing can act at all, so tickets simply pause until health checks pass, and an alert tells DevOps.

lab.title: Kill the VM at step 4
needs: The course repo at ~/Projects/ai-agents-course (the lab starts from the p7-4 lab's files)
lab.goal: Make a Temporal run survive a VM that freezes at step 4, continuing from the last checkpoint commit on a fresh VM, and stop to call a person when a second VM dies.

guess.q: A VM freezes during step 4 of 6. Steps 1 to 3 pushed checkpoint commits. With runWithRecovery, where does the fresh VM start?

options.text: At step 1 on main, because a fresh VM has nothing on its disk
options.why: The disk is empty, but the branch is not: freshen checks out the last checkpoint commit.

options.text: At step 4, from the commit pushed after step 3
options.why: Only the unfinished part of step 4 is lost. The code of steps 1 to 3 is on the branch, and the run knows the checkpoint from the heartbeat.

options.text: In the middle of step 4, exactly where the old VM stopped
options.why: Work after the last checkpoint was never saved outside the dead VM, so step 4 starts again from its beginning.

lab.build: Replace runInSandbox in workflows.mjs with runWithRecovery and call it from buildTicket. In a loop: claim a VM, freshen it at state.checkpoint?.sha ?? base, and work from (state.checkpoint?.step ?? 0) + 1. In catch, rethrow anything that is not an ActivityFailure whose cause is an ApplicationFailure of type SandboxDead; otherwise keep the checkpoint the dead VM reported (failure.details[0]), count the lost VM, and on the second loss notify and throw a non-retryable NeedsPerson failure. Release the VM in finally. Restart the worker, run node setup.mjs && node start.mjs, then try two deaths: stop the worker and start it with DEATHS=2 node worker.mjs.
checks: With one death, node start.mjs prints result: all 6 steps done on i-0002.
The worker log shows i-0002 freshened at the commit of step 3 and starting with step 4, not step 1.
git -C origin.git log --oneline nova/RH-1234 shows six wip commits, one per step, and no step twice.
With DEATHS=2, the run fails with two lost VMs and the worker prints the Slack message that names the branch.
Every claimed VM has a destroyed line in the worker log, the dead ones included.
lab.fix: A teammate thought the checkpoint record "could be stale", so they changed freshen to always use base. Make the same change (freshenSandbox(vm, base) and workInSandbox(vm, 1)), restart the worker and run node setup.mjs && node start.mjs. The run still succeeds, but the worker log shows i-0002 starting at step 1, and the branch history now has every early step twice, because the fresh VM redid two hours of work. Put the checkpoint back.
explain: Why does the harness push a checkpoint after each step whose checks pass, and not on a timer?
Why is a dead VM always destroyed and replaced, never restarted and reused?
Why does the run stop after the second lost VM instead of trying a third time?
lab.done: One frozen VM costs only step 4, two frozen VMs end the run with a message that names the branch, and you stopped the worker and the dev server.

check.q: Nova's VM froze in step 4. Which of these is lost?

options.why: Everything up to the last checkpoint is on the branch and in the runs bucket, and the conversation is in the session store.

options.text: Steps 1 to 4, because they were done on that VM
options.why: Steps 1 to 3 were pushed as checkpoint commits after their checks passed, so they live outside the VM.

options.text: The conversation, so the model must read everything again
options.why: The session store mirrored the transcript as it went, so the new VM resumes the same session.

check.q: Why does runWithRecovery freshen the new VM at the checkpoint sha and not at main?

options.text: Because main is protected and cannot be checked out on a VM
options.why: Any commit can be checked out. The point is which commit holds the work.

options.text: Because the checkpoint commit holds the steps that already passed, so the run continues instead of starting over
options.why: Freshening at main would throw away every step since the plan.

options.text: Because the broker refuses to fetch main for an agent
options.why: The broker scopes pushes to the run's branch; reading main is normal. The reason is not to lose work.

check.q: A ticket's second VM dies at the same step. What should happen?

options.text: Claim a third VM, since recovery is automatic
options.why: Two losses in a row on one ticket are a pattern, and a third VM would most likely die the same way.

options.text: Restart the second VM and try again on it
options.why: A dead VM is never reused, because nobody knows what state it is in.

options.text: Stop the run, keep the branch and notes, and hand the ticket back to the requester with a message that says where they are
options.why: The ticket needs a person, and nothing is lost: the person starts from the last checkpoint.

p: The checkpoint lives in ai-agents/harness/src/checkpoint.ts and runs after each step whose checks pass, and through nova-worker checkpoint on a Spot warning or before a parked VM is retired at 72 hours. Commits go to nova/RH-1234 through the broker's git proxy; notes.md and checkpoints/<n>.json go to s3://rhino-ai-agents-runs/runs/<run_id>/, and screenshots, traces and logs go to artifacts/ as they are made.

runWithRecovery in orchestrator/src/workflows/recovery.ts is used by both ticketToPr and routineRun. It counts ai_agents_vm_dead_total and ai_agents_recoveries_total for the alerts (lesson g3-15), and the drills terminate a real VM mid-run to prove it (lesson g3-16). Outages go through notify and waitOutOutage, with the back-off of 15 minutes, 30 minutes, then every hour. The G3-27 sketch only calls notify on the second loss; G4-05 also assigns the ticket back when a run stops, so use handBack there.

tickets.why: Checkpoints: the wip commit with [skip ci], notes.md, the checkpoint record and artifacts as they are made.
Dead-house recovery: SandboxDead after 5 silent minutes, a fresh VM from the last checkpoint, stop at the second loss.
Outages: back off, pause after 15 minutes without Claude, resume by itself, Slack and Jira fallback.

words.plain: A saved point after a step whose checks passed: a commit on the run's branch plus notes in the runs bucket.
The error workInSandbox throws when a VM stops sending heartbeats for 5 minutes or fails its status check.
Prepare a VM's checkout at a given commit: main for a new run, the last checkpoint after a recovery.
The loop that replaces a dead VM with a fresh one from the last checkpoint, and stops after the second loss.

review.q: From memory: the three things that leave the VM at a checkpoint, and where each one goes.
review.a: The code as a wip commit on nova/RH-1234 through the broker; notes.md and the checkpoint record in the runs bucket; the checkpoint sha in the heartbeat. The transcript is already in the session store.

review.q: The second VM died and a person opens the ticket. Why do the notes in the runs bucket matter, when the session transcript is saved too?
review.a: notes.md says in plain words what the plan is, what is done and what is next, so a person (or a later fresh run) can continue from step 4 in minutes. The transcript is long and written for the model.

review.q: A teammate wants MAX_LOST_VMS = 10 "to be robust". What do you answer?
review.a: Two losses in a row on one ticket point to a cause in the ticket or the step, so more tries only burn VMs. Stopping keeps the branch and notes, and a person continues from the checkpoint.

remember: Save outside the VM after every good step, replace a dead VM from the last checkpoint, and let the second loss call a person.
